text:
Kai M: heads-up — after we pushed toolkit-12 images to the eu-west GPU pool, a handful of training pods started failing with 'Illegal instruction' from the jit-compiled kernels. noticed ~0300UTC.

Priya S: seeing the same on gpu-eu-23. kernel logs show an oops followed by a hung NCCL all-reduce. suspect mixed libstdc++/glibc ABI from the builder toolchain.

Elle (infra): @Kai M @Priya S can you paste the container logs + node dmesg? also which image tag did we roll to?

Kai M: image tag is redwood/toolkit:12.0.1-prod. failing job id: training/bert-fp16-rl-004. excerpt:

```
E tensorflow: CPU device illegal instruction
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  failed to load kernel: cuLaunchKernel() -> illegal instruction
```

Priya S: node dmesg:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.456792] kernel: BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref at 0000000000000000
[  123.456795] nvlink: nccl: hang in all-reduce, pid=4221
```

ops-bot: deployment redwood/toolkit:12.0.1-prod -> eu-west-gpu started by @deploy-bot at 1767122000

James R: quick note — we built toolkit:12 images with gcc-13 on builders (to get newer optimizations). host nodes still on distro gcc-11 libs. that mismatch can produce ABI differences for C++ symbols and inline asm.

Sandeep: confirmed: the image has libstdc++.so.6 from gcc-13 (SONAME compatible but different symbol resolution). When the kernel picks JIT kernels compiled with that, some CPU features get emitted that aren't present on older host libs.

Anya: are we sure it's not a driver mismatch? driver on nodes is 520.xx (stable). toolkit-12 recommends >=525 for best support.

Priya S: we have two failure modes: 1) user containers crash with illegal instruction (likely compiler-generated insns); 2) nodes panic/oops when the driver interacts with newly compiled kernels — that looks like a driver/runtime ABI edge.

Elle (infra): immediate mitigation options:
- roll back image -> toolkit:11.8.* across eu-west (fast, small blast radius)
- cordon/drain suspicious nodes and run smoke tests with toolkit:12 locally (safer)
- rebuild toolkit:12 images using gcc-11 toolchain (longer)

Kai M: i started a partial rollback on the lowest-latency pool (eu-west-gpu-frontend) to reduce user impact. ops-bot please abort current rolling update for remaining nodes.

ops-bot: rolling-update eu-west-gpu canceled by @Kai M (1767123120)

James R: we should also add a preflight CI that runs a tiny job with host-driver combo to catch illegal instruction early. Will sketch a smoke matrix: (driver, cuda-toolkit, builder-gcc).

Sandeep: rebuilding 1k images with gcc-11 will add ~48h to release and consume our build runners. cost estimate: extra ~1.1k runner-hours and some spot churn. but it's the safest long term fix.

Anya: for short-term, can we push an ld-preload shim that forces the container to use host libstdc++? risky but faster.

Priya S: we tried preload shim on a dev node — it prevented the illegal instruction in one case, but node-level oops still occurred in another. so it's a partial bandaid.

Elle (infra): decision for now:
1) complete rollback to toolkit:11.8 on eu-west pools (finish within 30m) — reduces user failures.
2) cordon gpu-eu-23 and gpu-eu-24, run hardware diagnostics and full dmesg/kernel-analysis.
3) schedule image rebuilds with gcc-11 and add the driver-toolkit preflight CI into merge gates.
4) ops to write incident follow-up doc with cost impact and timeline.

Kai M: i'll open an internal incident and tag oncall + infra-sre. add affected customer notes (some enterprise customers hit inference latency spikes).

Anya: i'm running a canary rebuild now with gcc-11 and running the NCCL stress test. i'll post results.

James R: long-term: add a 'builder toolchain pin' metadata to images and enforce a compatibility matrix (builder-gcc, cuda-toolkit, host-driver). prevents surprise ABI/ISA mismatches.

Priya S: thanks all. we'll keep the thread updated. ping @ops-bot for rollback completion and @Elle (infra) for follow-up doc link. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rollback to redwood/toolkit:11.8.7-prod completed on eu-west-gpu at 1767123789 (rolled back 18 nodes)

Elle (infra): created postmortem draft: https://corp.redwood/notes/incident-1767123456-toolkit-toolchain-compat (will add timelines + cost)

Anya: can confirm canary gcc-11 build passes NCCL stress and no illegal-instruction observed so far.

Kai M: closing loop — we revert the production rollout, cordoned nodes are under investigation, and image rebuild + CI gating is next. thanks team.
